lesson_title: One Message, a Chain of Forwards: Geometric Sequences
hook_text: Three people get a message. Each forwards it to four more. By round eight it reaches a small city — here is the formula that counts it.
clip_script: A message reaches 3 people. Each of them forwards it to 4 more. Round one: 3 readers. Round two: 12. Round three: 48. To know round eight you do not trudge through the rounds — take the start, 3, and apply the multiplier 4 seven times. That is the general term: a times r to the power n minus one. Seven, not eight, because round one is the launch, and forwarding only begins after it. Now feel the difference between adding and multiplying. Adding 4 seven times gives 28 more readers. Multiplying by 4 seven times gives a factor of sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty-four — round eight reaches 49 152 people from a start of three. Multiplication does not climb; it detonates. And the formula runs backwards too: which round reaches exactly 3072? Divide by 3, recognise 1024 as 4 to the fifth, and n is 6. Round six. Same-base thinking, one line. That detonation is exactly how compound interest grows your money — same formula, wearing a suit.
visual_style: Phone screens lighting up in waves across a night-time city map, each wave four times wider than the last, a counter exploding upwards while an addition counter crawls beneath it.
pacing: Slow ticks for rounds one to three, accelerating bursts to round eight, calm landing on the backwards question.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and command the exponent behind every geometric sequence.
